channel.title: Wire — Engineering
channel.description: Engineering from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
item.description: OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Netflix at QConSF 2026: Retrofitting the SDLC for AI Coding Agents
item.description: At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mark Khuzam of Netflix explained how the Commerce team retrofitted its SDLC so AI coding agents and engineers could ship together. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Replaying merged changes: how we test whether a knowledge base makes coding agents better
item.description: Introduction Every session, you get a new teammate: a coding agent. It reads code faster than you and has seen more of it than your whole team put together. What it does not have is any memory of how your service got this way. (1 source: grab)

item.title: How Grab built Scarlet: the AI teammate that turns a Slack message into a production data pipeline
item.description: Introduction In the blog From firefighting to building , we described the agents our Analytics Data Warehouse (ADW) team built to take routine work off data engineers. Scarlet was the Enhancement Agent in that post. (1 source: grab)

item.title: Part 1: Simulation-first AI experimentation for ads at Grab
item.description: Introduction Ads delivery at Grab is increasingly an artificial intelligence (AI) decisioning problem. (1 source: grab)

item.title: Probing DNS at Cloudflare
item.description: At Cloudflare we’ve built tools to enable teams to extend our internal testing framework and build test tooling for networking protocols. This is the story of how this was used for DNS. (1 source: cloudflare)

item.title: Agoda Reduces API Code Review Time by 64% with Modular Architecture
item.description: Agoda introduced a modular monolith framework in its post-booking API to reduce coupling without a full rewrite. The platform uses domain components, Data Mapper patterns, typed builders, and ArchUnit tests to enforce boundaries. (1 source: infoq)
